PainEngine Launcher
Usage: EngineLauncher.exe <command> [arguments]
Without arguments: open the launcher GUI.

Commands:
  --help
  -h
  /?
  --create-project <NEW-folder> <name>
  --enable-code <Project.json>
  --build-project <Project.json>
  --install-engine <Runtime-folder>
  --upgrade-project <Project.json> <NEW-copy-folder>
  --check-project <Project.json>
  --smoke-project <Project.json>
  --smoke-project-editor <Project.json>
  --smoke-project-current <Project.json>
  --smoke-project-editor-current <Project.json>
  --smoke-project-prompt <Project.json>
  --smoke-project-editor-prompt <Project.json>
  --check <example>
  --smoke <example>
  --check-editor <example>
  --smoke-editor <example>

Create a C++ project (the parent folder must exist):
  EngineLauncher.exe --create-project "E:\Games\MyCity" "My City"
  EngineLauncher.exe --enable-code "E:\Games\MyCity\Project.json"
  EngineLauncher.exe --build-project "E:\Games\MyCity\Project.json"
  EngineLauncher.exe --smoke-project "E:\Games\MyCity\Project.json"
The project folder must be NEW, even if an existing folder is empty.
C++ requires Visual Studio C++ tools, Windows SDK and the pinned engine's SDK.
Build diagnostics: CodeBuild.log in the project folder.
Default project smoke uses the pinned engine; -current uses this launcher's Runtime.
Smoke runs 3 frames. Only -prompt smoke options display the upgrade dialog.
Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operation failed, 2 invalid command/arguments/example.
Output: stdout for help; stderr for errors; redirected text is UTF-8.
PowerShell: use Start-Process -Wait -PassThru (GUI executable); read ExitCode.
Guide: Engine/docs/LAUNCHER-CLI.md
